clue.text: Virile plebeian?

definitions.meaning: manly, vigorous and full of energy
a common person rather than a blue-blooded aristocrat

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: a commoner has ordinary red blood, not the blue blood of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a vigorous, lusty man, and someone of common birth, as opposed to blue-blooded.

clue.text: Rub out earlier expression in a note

parts.note: ex- means former or earlier
a term is a word or expression
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone erases a phrase they had previously written in a short letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out someone is slang for killing them, which is to destroy or wipe out.

clue.text: Musicians ready — then not allowed in audition?

parts.note: ready and brass are both British slang for cash or money

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for not allowed is to be heard spoken

parts.note: something not allowed is banned

explanation.surface: Musicians arrive prepared, only to be refused at their tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not the adjective but slang for money, like BRASS; BANNED spoken sounds like BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of players of trumpets, cornets and tubas is a band of musicians.

clue.text: 'Crooked-Nose" the sprite, in person

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of the following word are twisted

parts.note: an elf is a sprite or fairy

explanation.surface: A fairy nicknamed Crooked-Nose appears in the flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress 'Crooked-Nose' up as a fairy's nickname; in fact 'Crooked' is an instruction to bend the next word into ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneself is one's own person, the individual self.

clue.text: Criminal activity in the Sun? It's a ridiculous charge

definitions.meaning: theft carried out by day, as if in sunlight, read literally
an outrageously excessive price asked for something

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: robbing in broad day; the Sun may suggest a newspaper report of crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a blatant overcharging, and literally it is theft committed in broad sunshine.

clue.text: See? I do see, struggling with chapter

indicators.note: the chapter letter is taken in among the jumbled letters, kept with them
struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters of the three preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A speaker insists they understand while wrestling with a section of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an exclamation but is the definition, a bishop's area; 'struggling' makes DIOESE, which 'with' then splits to take the chapter letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under that bishop's authority.

clue.text: Discarded tools may be kept in one

definitions.meaning: cast off or got rid of, as a snake does its skin

definitions.text: tools may be kept in one
definitions.meaning: a garden hut where spades and mowers are stored

explanation.definitionFit: A snake that has cast off its skin has discarded it; a small garden outbuilding stores tools.

clue.text: Haircut Italian got in Western part of island

indicators.note: got in means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the word hair cut short loses its last letter
It is short for Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A trim from an Italian barber was had on the west side of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haircut' is read as HAIR cut, losing its R; 'got in' puts IT inside, between A and I.
explanation.definitionFit: This republic occupies the western third of Hispaniola in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Fantasy Disney originally put down on paper

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is set on top of the second
originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A Disney fantasy story is first sketched out on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is an imagined vision, a fantasy of the mind.

clue.text: Military's policy's off course, but about to obtain backing

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to stray is to wander off course

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the verb is written backwards

parts.note: to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: An army's plan has gone wrong, but it is about to win support.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma-free surface reads as a failing army; 'backing' makes TEG, and 'about' is the container signal, not a word meaning nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategy is the overall planning of a military campaign.

clue.text: Like some fish that are caught using the net?

definitions.text: Like some fish that are caught

explanation.definitionFit: A hooked fish is on the angler's line, and a person browsing is connected to the internet.

clue.text: Survivor got out of wreck, of course

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, so the letters of the last word are broken apart

explanation.surface: Of course someone came out of the shipwreck alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is the castaway hero of Defoe's novel who survived a shipwreck.

clue.text: One has belief in God, involving most of all the hope of perfection

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: deism is belief in a creator God

indicators.note: most of means the word that follows loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A believer in God puts their faith in the hope that things will be perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of all' reads as 'above everything' but is a trim giving AL; 'involving' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is the pursuit of high principles, aiming at a perfect state.

clue.text: Part of England mentioned in fatuous passages read aloud?

indicators.note: read aloud says the phrase is to be heard, so the spoken form gives the answer

parts.note: fatuous means silly, and passages between seats are aisles

explanation.surface: An English region gets a mention in some foolish texts recited to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scilly Isles are an English island group off the far south-west tip of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isles of Scilly form an archipelago belonging to the county of Cornwall in England.

clue.text: Site of historic listed building

parts.note: listed suggests a protected heritage building, but here it means leaning over, like a ship that lists

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a listed building is protected by law; here 'listed' means tilted, as a ship lists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is home to the famous leaning bell tower, a building that tilts.

clue.text: Scale in F — hear the variation

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical scale in the key of F, played with a variation for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges INFHEARTHE; 'Scale in F' looks musical but 'in F' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the temperature scale on which water freezes at 32 degrees.

clue.text: Variety act that could have host in my power, in short?

indicators.note: could have signals the letters might be rearranged into another form

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A stage turn in which a performer might bring the presenter under their control.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage mesmerism, putting volunteers into a trance, was a staple turn in music halls.

clue.text: This gives the plot of affairs of the heart

definitions.text: This gives the plot of affairs of the heart

parts.words: This gives the plot of affairs of the heart
parts.note: plot reads as a story of romance, but it means a graph tracing heart activity

explanation.definitionFit: A medical trace records the electrical workings of the heart as a graph.

clue.text: Tragic hero excessively cut up over torment with love

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over what follows
in a down clue, up means the piece reads from the bottom, backwards
cut means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: too means excessively
hell is torment
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A doomed protagonist is terribly distressed by the agony of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims TOO to TO and 'up' turns it to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice is the tragic hero of the play bearing his name.

clue.text: Great service I have

parts.note: Mass is a church service
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A speaker has had a wonderful church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means huge, an extension of great in the sense of big.

clue.text: Cover piano completely

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, softly
all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: A dust sheet covers the whole piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pall is a cloth draped over a coffin, so a cover.

clue.text: European not missed in India?

parts.note: not missed reads as not regretted, but means not a Miss, so a married European lady in the Raj

explanation.walkthrough: In British India a married European woman was addressed with this title, not as Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was used in colonial India for a married white woman.

clue.text: Daughter brought in by, say, dinner gong

indicators.note: brought in by means taken inside the next piece

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal, the say marking the example

explanation.surface: A daughter is called to the table by the sounding of the dinner gong.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal; 'say' shows dinner is one kind of meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for an award, especially a decoration worn on the chest.

clue.text: Complaint from mother over words added to letter

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over the second

parts.note: mum is mother
PS, a postscript, is words added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Mum writes an afterthought at the bottom of her letter, full of grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a viral illness, and a complaint is an ailment.

clue.text: Wooden cube, for example, holding tons

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a cube is an example of a solid shape

explanation.surface: A block of wood, cube-shaped, weighs tons.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive and unexpressive, like a wooden manner.

clue.text: Girl Guide returned, having secured female title

indicators.note: having secured means holding on to, so one piece encloses the other
returned means sent back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to lead is to guide
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide comes back having won a women's championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guide' looks like one unit, but Girl is the definition and Guide the start of the wordplay; 'returned' makes DAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old word for a young woman or maiden.

clue.text: Match-fit?

parts.note: reads as ready to play a game, but means suitable for a marriage match

explanation.definitionFit: An eligible bachelor is considered a suitable partner for marriage.

clue.text: Stay later than the others

explanation.definitionFit: To last is to endure, and the last one comes after all the rest.

clue.text: What high-fliers look for when the pressure eases?

definitions.text: What high-fliers look for when the pressure eases?

parts.words: What high-fliers look for when the pressure eases?
parts.note: high-fliers suggests ambitious executives seeking relief from stress, but means air travellers needing breathing help when cabin pressure drops

explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft drop breathing apparatus for passengers if cabin pressure falls.
